description: Figure 8 illustrates the convergence of shared Top-6 routed experts between two independent samples of a task as a function of sample size. The x-axis, labeled “Sample Size,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2¹⁰ (1,024) to 2¹⁷ (131,072), with major tick marks at powers of two (2¹⁰, 2¹¹, ..., 2¹⁷). The y-axis, labeled “Shared Top-6 Routed Experts (Averaged by Model Layers),” is linear and ranges from 0 to 6, with tick marks at integer intervals (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), representing the average number of experts selected in the Top-6 across all model layers that are common between the two samples. The plot contains a single solid black line with circular markers, which starts near y = 2.5 at x = 2¹⁰, rises steeply through x = 2¹³, and then plateaus near y = 5.5 as sample size increases beyond 2¹⁵, indicating that the expert selection stabilizes and becomes highly consistent between samples once sufficient data is available.
